# Opus V3 integrated revision (parent: V2)

**Status and provenance.** This is a researcher-assisted, modern revision round. It uses aircraft-dynamics concepts that were not in the 1898 packet: AVL/VLM, stability derivatives, characteristic roots and inertia tensors. Every number here falls into one of four categories:

- **[A] design assumption:** my chosen or assumed value.
- **[C] calculation:** hand arithmetic by me, or an evaluator result quoted with its source.
- **[M] measured:** there are none in this round.
- **UNKNOWN:** each comes with the test that would resolve it.

No wind-tunnel, flight or weighing result exists. The concept is not proposed for crewed flight or construction clearance.

## 1. What changed and why

The evaluator found four gaps:

- The V2 alpha–q reduced screen passes only as a sign test.
- Body, fin and installed propulsion/control effects are missing.
- Engine margin is thin: 11.67 kW demand against an unverified 13 kW.
- No full mode set exists.

V3 therefore makes a small set of mutually consistent changes rather than a static-margin retune.

| ID | Item | V2 (parent) | V3 | Reason | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Propeller definition | radius 1.2, 2 blades, rpm/ratio UNKNOWN | Adopt V6: D 2.4 m, 2 blades, 400 rpm, 2.5:1 chain (engine 1000 rpm), ω = +41.888 x̂ rad/s (x aft) | Mechanically compatible: same disc x = 2.1, hub z = 0.9, radius and mass | Enables J, C_T, C_P, torque and gyroscopic terms. The V6 blade sections are unscreened and 7 of 8 chords are missing, so prop performance stays UNKNOWN. |
| R2 | Fin | LE x 4.80, chord 0.80, fin 1.12 m², 3 kg | LE x 4.50, chord 1.10 (z 0.60–2.00), fin 1.54 m², 4 kg; rudder unchanged 0.66 m² | Fin volume 0.020 → 0.025 [C]. Counters the destabilising forward nacelle and pusher disc side force. | +1 kg; CG +0.011 m aft; see §2 |
| R3 | Fuel ledger | E3 15 kg combined | E3a tank 4 kg + E3b fuel 0–11 kg [A] | Fuel extremes needed | CG envelope defined |
| R4 | Operator extremes | 70 kg only | 60 / 70 / 85 kg [A] | CG envelope | See §2 |
| R5 | Sign conventions | V1 control signs | Retained, plus explicit mapping to standard body/stability axes and standard control signs | Evaluator's elevator sign was ambiguous | Mapping below |
| R6 | Control rate limits | none | Assumed surface-rate limits and cable-stretch allowance [A] | Required for the full gate | Measurement required |
| R7 | Mass properties | inertia UNKNOWN | Intrinsic inertia per component from stated shapes; assembled tensor [C] | Gate item 1 | Estimate only; the swing test in §8 must replace it |

**Rejected options (retained for the record):**
- **Lower the thrust line to cut the −0.44 N m/N power–pitch coupling.** Rejected. The prop tip would drop below the V2 0.6 m ground and 0.472 m at 13° clearances.
- **Raise dihedral pre-emptively.** Kept as a conditional fix only (§7), because the spiral root is unknown.
- **Nose ballast to raise margin.** Conditional only (§7). It costs payload and power.
- **Adopt V5A blade sections.** Rejected; they are unscreened.

## 2. Coordinate schedule and mass

**Frames.**
- **Design frame F_D (unchanged).** Origin at the lower-wing LE on the centreline; x aft, y starboard, z up. This frame is right-handed, and +M_y is nose-up.
- **Dynamics frame F_S.** Standard stability axes at the CG: x_s forward along trim V, y_s starboard, z_s down. The transformation is (x_s, y_s, z_s) = (−(x − x_cg), y, −(z − z_cg)), then rotated by trim α.
- **Control signs in F_S (standard).** δe positive TE-down. δa positive for right-flap TE-up / left TE-down (right roll). δr positive TE-port (nose-left, standard). The mappings from V3 signs are δe_std = −δe_V3, δa_std = δ_flap,stbd,V3, and δr_std = −δr_V3.
- **Inertia convention.** I_ij are the positive-definite tensor components. Products are defined as I_xz = ∫x z dm, and the equations of motion use −I_xz off-diagonal.

**Three-view schedule** (F_D; port mirrors y → −y):
- **Wings.** Lower wing: rectangle, chord 1.8, LE x 0, z 0 at |y| ≤ 1.6, rising to 0.0681 at y 5.5. Upper wing: LE z 1.8 → 1.8681 at y 5.5. Flaps: x 1.35–1.80, y 3.5–5.5.
- **Nacelle.** Box x −1.6…0.2, |y| ≤ 0.35, z −0.35…0.40.
- **Propeller.** Disc x 2.1, centre z 0.9, R 1.2.
- **Booms.** From (1.35, ±1.6, 0.05) and (1.35, ±1.6, 1.2) to (4.5, ±1.6, 0.6), then to (5.6, ±1.6, 0.6).
- **Tailplane.** x 4.5–5.6, |y| ≤ 2.2, z 0.6. Elevator x 5.6–6.1, cut-out |y| ≤ 0.25.
- **Fin (V3).** x 4.5–5.6, z 0.6–2.0 at y 0. Rudder x 5.6–6.1, z 0.68–2.0.
- **Skids.** x −1.9…1.6, y ±0.95. Tail skid at x 5.5.

**Mass and CG** [A masses, C sums]:
- Nominal configuration (pilot 70 kg, full fuel 11 kg): m = 361 kg, Σm·x = 225.915, Σm·z = 167.233. CG = (0.6258, 0, 0.4633).

| Case | Pilot / fuel (kg) | m (kg) | x_cg | z_cg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nominal | 70 / 11 | 361 | 0.6258 | 0.4633 |
| Forward-heavy | 85 / 11 | 376 | 0.5649 | 0.4567 |
| Aft-light, empty tank | 60 / 0 | 340 | 0.6748 | 0.4636 |
| Aft, full fuel | 60 / 11 | 351 | 0.6693 | 0.4640 |

**Static margin.** The neutral point from the evaluator's 7.76% diagnostic at x 0.6148 is x_NP ≈ 0.7545 [C, derived]. The V2 VLM shift gave 0.724. Margins are listed as evaluator-based / V2-based:

| Case | Margin (evaluator NP / V2 NP) |
|---|---|
| Nominal | 7.1% / 5.4% |
| Aft-light | 4.4% / 2.7% |
| Forward | 10.6% / 8.9% |

Estimated C_mα at the nominal CG is −0.286 + 3.747 × (0.011/1.8) ≈ **−0.263/rad** [C]. It must be recomputed.

**Inertia.** Each component has an intrinsic inertia from an idealised shape (JSON), and the tensor is assembled by the parallel-axis theorem about the nominal CG [C]:

| Component | Value (kg m²) |
|---|---|
| Ixx | ≈ 1130 |
| Iyy | ≈ 1047 |
| Izz | ≈ 1881 |
| I_xz | ≈ +103 (same sign in F_D and F_S body axes) |
| Ixy, Iyz | 0 by symmetry |

- The triangle inequalities hold.
- Uncertainty is roughly ±25%. The largest uncertain contributors are the nacelle shell factor, the operator, the blade mass split and the boom distribution.
- Propeller angular momentum is h_p ≈ 4.21 × 41.89 ≈ **176 kg m²/s along +x_D (aft)** [C].

## 3. Installed surfaces and controls

**Elevator**
- Hinge from (5.6, ±2.2, 0.6); chord 0.5.
- Travel −15/+20° (V3 +, TE-up). Assumed rate limit 60°/s [A].
- Column ±0.15 m; pull gives TE-up.
- Envelope: TE z 0.471–0.771, ground clearance 1.371.
- Cable stretch allowance ±1° [A].

**Balancing flaps**
- Hinge (1.35, ±3.5, 1.884) to (1.35, ±5.5, 1.919); chord 0.45.
- Travel ±15°, opposed. Assumed rate 60°/s [A].
- Wheel right gives starboard flap TE-up.
- Clearance: TE Δz ±0.116; outside the prop disc (|y| ≥ 3.5 > 1.2).

**Rudder**
- Hinge (5.6, 0, 0.68) to (5.6, 0, 2.0); chord 0.5.
- Travel ±25°. Assumed rate 50°/s [A].
- Right pedal gives V3 +, TE-port.
- Clearance: TE y ±0.211, 0.06 m above the torque tube.
- The rudder is not affected by R2. The fin now ends at the hinge line, and the fin LE at x 4.5 lies 2.4 m aft of the disc.

**Fin and body**
- Fin LE post at (4.5, 0, 0.6–2.0), carried on the tailplane front spar between the boom junctions (4.5, ±1.6, 0.6).
- Two bracing wires run from the fin top to BU0 (1.35, ±1.6, 1.2) and are included in the 4 kg.
- Nacelle side area ≈ 1.8 × 0.75 = 1.35 m², centroid x ≈ −0.7. This is destabilising in yaw by roughly −1.35 × 1.33 m of lever against the fin's 2.2 m² at ≈ 4.8 m [C, crude]. The installed Cn_β is UNKNOWN.

**Propeller installed effects**
- Disc side force per β (P-factor/N_β): UNKNOWN.
- Slipstream: the prop is a pusher ahead of the tail, so the wake washes the fin and tailplane. The wake-on-tail dynamic pressure ratio is UNKNOWN.
- Torque reaction: about 280–300 N m right-wing-down at 13 kW (assuming ≈ 0.95 chain efficiency) [C].
- Flap roll authority against this torque is UNKNOWN.

**Hinge moments, stick forces and friction:** UNKNOWN.

## 4. Propulsion, drag and trim

**Operating point at 15 m/s** [C]:
- n = 6.667 rev/s, J = 0.9375, tip helical speed ≈ 52.5 m/s.
- Geometric pitch at r = 0.6 is 2.90 m (P/D = 1.21).
- Required thrust T = 448 N gives C_T = 0.248.
- At 11.67 kW shaft power, C_P = 0.404, so η = 0.575.
- Momentum-theory ideal efficiency is 0.866. This is an upper bound, not an estimate.

**Drag scenarios.** Parasite drag is scaled from the V2 inference, CD0 ≈ 0.050 on 38 m². Induced drag is 185 N. Propeller efficiency is 0.575 [A] and chain efficiency 0.95 [A].

| Scenario | Parasite (N) | Total drag (N) | Shaft power (kW) | Engine power (kW) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (0.8×) | 209 | 394 | 10.3 | 10.8 |
| Nominal | 261 | 446.5 | 11.65 | 12.3 |
| High (1.3×) | 340 | 525 | 13.7 | 14.4 |

The high-drag scenario exceeds the 13 kW target. The nominal case leaves only about 6% margin and no climb margin. **This is a no-go until measured.**

**Trim strategy.**
- **Thrust moment.** The thrust line sits 0.437 m above the nominal CG, giving −0.437 N m per N of thrust (nose-down).
- **Power-on at 15 m/s.** Thrust moment −196 N m; tail download; V2 estimate δe ≈ +3.4° TE-up (range 2.3–7.0).
- **Power-off glide.** Removing the thrust moment gives a nose-up change. With the V2 C_mδ ≈ 0.011/deg (±50%), about 104 N m per degree at 15 m/s, the trim shifts by about −1.9° (TE-down) at equal speed [C].
- **Glide speed and angle.** UNKNOWN. The glide angle estimate is CD/CL ≈ 0.128, about 7.3° [C].
- **Tests required.** Trim must be solved, not extrapolated, at every §5 state for both power-on and power-off. Elevator reserve of at least 5° beyond trim in both directions is a proposed design gate.

## 5. Derivative analysis and test matrix

**States:**

| State | Condition |
|---|---|
| S1 | 15 m/s, nominal CG, power-on |
| S2 | 15 m/s, aft-light CG, power-on |
| S3 | 15 m/s, forward CG, power-on |
| S4 | 13 m/s, aft CG, power-on (stall margin UNKNOWN; include the S1 section stall check) |
| S5 | 18 m/s, nominal CG, power-on |
| S6 | Power-off glide, nominal and aft CG |
| S7 | S1 with ±20% thrust |

**Methods and resolving tests:**
- **Steady AVL/VLM on V3 geometry with nacelle and fin modelled.** Longitudinal derivatives: C_Lα, C_mα, C_Lq, C_mq, C_Du (via polar). Lateral derivatives: C_Yβ, C_lβ, C_nβ, C_Yp, C_lp, C_np, C_Yr, C_lr, C_nr. Control derivatives: C_Lδe, C_mδe, C_lδa, C_nδa (adverse yaw), C_Yδr, C_nδr, C_lδr.
- **Body.** Nacelle and skid contributions from a panel model or slender-body estimate, then a towed or wind-tunnel measurement of the nacelle.
- **C_Lα̇ and C_mα̇.** These cannot come from steady AVL. Two routes:
  - (a) An analytic downwash-lag model, C_mα̇ ≈ −2 a_t η_t V_H (l_t/c)(dε/dα), labelled an estimate. Its inputs dε/dα and η_t are taken from the AVL wake.
  - (b) An unsteady VLM (frequency-domain) run, confirmed by a forced-oscillation test of a scale model.
  - Until then, run a sweep over C_mα̇ ∈ [−15, 0] and C_Lα̇ ∈ [0, 4]. This range is an assumption to be bounded, not a value.
- **Propulsion.**
  - X_u from dT/dV. This needs a BEM analysis of the V6 blade, which requires the chords.
  - Thrust moment derivative M_T = −0.437 N m/N.
  - Slipstream effects on tail η_t and on dε/dα.
  - Disc normal force derivatives N_β and N_α.
  - Gyroscopic coupling h_p = 176 kg m²/s.
  - Torque reaction.
  - All need a static and towed prop-stand test and a smoke/yarn wake survey on the tail.
- **Flap and hinge.** Hinge moment coefficients measured on a surface rig. Adverse yaw C_nδa measured in tow tests.

## 6. Root calculation path

**Longitudinal model.** States [u, w, q, θ] in F_S (stability axes). Full A matrix including X_u, X_w, Z_u, Z_w, Z_ẇ, Z_q, M_u, M_w, M_ẇ, M_q, gravity θ₀ terms and thrust derivatives. Solve the quartic for its four roots.
- Mode labels are assigned from eigenvectors: short period (α, q dominant) and phugoid (u, θ dominant).

**Lateral model.** States [β, p, r, φ] with the I_xz coupling, using I′ terms. Four roots.
- Mode labels: roll subsidence (p dominant), spiral (φ, r, slow real), Dutch roll (β, r oscillatory).

**Reported outputs.** For each root: λ, ζ, ω_n, period, and time to half (or double) amplitude.

**Uncertainty sweep.** Monte Carlo over:
- Inertia ±25%
- All aerodynamic derivatives ±30%
- The C_mα̇/C_Lα̇ range above
- η_t 0.8–1.3
- The CG envelope

**Existing conditional arithmetic** (not a verdict):
- Evaluator reduced α–q numbers with my Iyy = 1047 give Mα ≈ −2.58 s⁻² and Mq ≈ −3.59 s⁻¹.
- The resulting reduced roots are λ ≈ −3.59 ± 1.32i (ω_n ≈ 3.82 rad/s, ζ ≈ 0.94).
- This excludes α̇ terms, body, propulsion and the V3 CG.
- A Lanchester phugoid approximation gives ω ≈ √2 g/U ≈ 0.92 rad/s (period ≈ 6.8 s) and ζ ≈ 0.09.
- These are hypotheses only.

**Lateral roots:** all UNKNOWN. Qualitative risks:
- Weak dihedral (1°) and the pusher layout make spiral divergence plausible.
- Lightly damped Dutch roll is plausible if the nacelle dominates.

## 7. Conditional fixes (applied only if the sweep shows the problem)

- **Spiral time to double < 20 s.**
  - Change: outer-panel dihedral from 1° to 3°, raising the tip from 0.068 to 0.204 m on both wings.
  - Mass: ≈ 0 kg.
  - Lift and power: C_L falls by about 0.1%, negligible.
  - Side effects: wire lengths change; wing
